hints.message: categories.parent_id has a foreign key but no index that starts with it, so deleting or updating a category row scans the whole table.
comments.user_id has a foreign key but no index that starts with it, so deleting or updating a user row scans the whole table.
posts.user_id has a foreign key but no index that starts with it, so deleting or updating a user row scans the whole table.
role_user.role_id has a foreign key but no index that starts with it, so deleting or updating a role row scans the whole table.
taggables.tag_id has a foreign key but no index that starts with it, so deleting or updating a tag row scans the whole table.
users.country_id has a foreign key but no index that starts with it, so deleting or updating a country row scans the whole table.

taggables has no primary key, so one row cannot be updated or deleted reliably and some replication setups refuse the table. Add a composite primary key on (taggable_type, taggable_id, tag_id) so a pair cannot be attached twice.
comments_user_id_foreign links comments to users, but no model declares a relation for it.
Category::posts() and Post::category() use posts.category_id, which has no foreign key to categories, so rows can point to a category that no longer exists.
Laranex\LaravelSchemaViewer\Tests\Fixtures\Models\Ghost uses the ghosts table, which does not exist on the testing connection.
comments.commentable_type stores class names such as Laranex\LaravelSchemaViewer\Tests\Fixtures\Models\Post, so renaming a model breaks existing rows. Map them with Relation::enforceMorphMap().
taggables.taggable_type stores class names such as Laranex\LaravelSchemaViewer\Tests\Fixtures\Models\Post, so renaming a model breaks existing rows. Map them with Relation::enforceMorphMap().
